notation: Two waves of one workgroup, 32 lanes each (lane l of either wave addresses the dword at LDS byte 4 l, so both waves touch the same 128 bytes; '@256' adds 256). A script is a list of: 'barrier' (the workgroup barrier), 'fence' (a barrier that is an LDS fence), [w, ops] (ops run by wave w only), ['all', ops] (by both). The core runs each wave to its next barrier in wave order, so between two barriers wave 0's ops run before wave 1's. Ops: read (a 4-byte LDS read), write (a 4-byte LDS write of 7), atomic (a 4-byte LDS add of 7), wait_ds / wait_ds(1) (the ds counter's wait with count 0 / 1), wait_vm (the load counter's wait, count 0), smem (a scalar load), end (the wave ends), store (the wave stores the dword it read to global memory; 'stored' gives the first 8 dwords), fence_sole / barrier_sole (a wave stops at that barrier alone). After the script every wave waits for all its counters and ends. error: the expected message with instruction texts replaced by op names (wording informative; the facts - which wave, which byte, which ops - required), or null.
